findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the class is defined. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit value gets the same process-start timestamp. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The `to_dict` test only checks that `queued` is not None, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: `to_dict` puts a raw datetime in the Celery task kwargs, which breaks serialization and the round trip
findings.body: `asdict(self)` leaves `queued` as a `datetime`. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict as `kwargs` to `apply_async`. With a JSON serializer the datetime is either rejected or turned into a string. The task then calls `from_dict`, which does `cls(**input_dict)`, so `queued` is a string rather than a datetime. Nothing checks this, and the type is silently wrong. `to_dict` should serialize the timestamp explicitly and `from_dict` should parse it.

findings.title: `from_dict` does not validate field types
findings.body: `from_dict` only catches `ValueError` and `TypeError`. A dict with correct keys but a wrong `integration_id` type is accepted without complaint. A malformed source then fails the equality check in `should_sync` quietly, and the cycle protection is skipped.

findings.title: `assignment_source` kwarg is passed to every integration's `sync_assignee_outbound`
findings.body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` signature accepts `**kwargs`, but other implementations (Jira, VSTS, GitHub and others) may not. Any that don't will raise `TypeError` and the outbound assignee sync will fail. Every implementation needs to be checked or updated. The PR also changes the `sync_status_outbound` abstract signature without touching its implementations.

findings.title: Inbound sync still not covered for other callers of `where_should_sync`
findings.body: `where_should_sync` calls `should_sync(key)` without a source. That is fine for this path. But `sync_group_assignee_inbound` builds the `AssignmentSource` from the `integration` argument, so the cycle break depends on `integration.id` matching `org_integration.integration_id`. If other assign paths do not pass an `assignment_source`, such as the Jira webhook handling or `sync_status_inbound`, the loop is still possible. The PR gives no evidence these are covered.

findings.title: No test for deassign with a matching source, or for another integration
findings.body: Only the `assign` path is tested with a matching-source integration. There is no test that `deassign` with a matching source skips the outbound sync. There is also no test that a different integration still syncs. The task-level serialization round trip through `to_dict`/`from_dict` is not covered by an assertion either.
